Subject: Re: Achilles sore after upping my k's - rest or push on?

Hey Mel — haven't seen your leg so I can't diagnose anything, but going from 30 to 48 km a week in three weeks is a big spike, and your description (morning stiffness, tenderness a few cm up from the heel, easing once you're running, a lump) fits the classic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy picture rather than a tear.

What I'd do with the running:

- Pull the kilometres back to where you were comfortable for a week or two, then build again more slowly. Don't keep pushing through the limping.
- Loading beats rest. Heel drops off a step are fine, but heavy slow calf raises (slow, controlled, straight knee) have better evidence behind them. On the days it feels angry, do isometric calf holds instead — a 45-60 second hold, a few times through.
- A heel lift in the shoe is a handy short-term trick to take the stretch out of it.

On pain: up to 3/10 while loading is fine, as long as it's settled by the next morning. If it's still 4-5/10 the next day or you're limping, back off the volume and the calf work.

On the stretching and the injection: stretching it hard until it burns isn't the way, that tends to keep the tendon irritated rather than settle it. Cortisone isn't recommended for this either — it doesn't address the load problem and can weaken the tendon, so if you'd rather avoid a needle, that's the better news.

When to get it seen: if it's not clearly improving in 3-4 weeks, book in with any sports physio. You're in Bayswater, so plenty of options close by — no need to wait for a particular place.

Get it checked urgently the same day (GP or ED) if you get a sudden pop, feel like you've been kicked in the back of the leg, or suddenly can't push off or can't do a single heel raise. That's a different problem and shouldn't sit on it.

One general thing worth knowing: some antibiotics, particularly the fluoroquinolone ones, have been linked with tendon problems and occasionally ruptures. If you're on or have recently been on one for something else, mention it to your GP.

Best of luck with the half in February — very doable if you rebuild the base properly.
